text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants top income tax rate of 35 percent and basic rate of 20 percent.
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer believes health insurance contributions will continue to rise.
- Candidate of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats wins election to become new mayor of Stuttgart.
- Ruling coalition agrees plans tax based on damage fuels do to the environment.
HANDELSBLATT
- Aircraft maker DASA ready to cut price of Eurofighter in bid to secure the future of the project.
- Engineering employers in combative mood after failure of wage talks in state of Baden-Wuerttemberg.
- Mitropa, catering unit of state railway operator Deutsche Bahn, plans to expand into other European rail networks.
- Investment fair in Duesseldorf records 20 percent increase in visitors this year.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Waigel wants to tax health and unemployment benefit payments.
- Bertelsmann plans to put television channels RTL, RTL 2 and Super RTL in one holding company.
- Miners' mood getting worse by the day, union leader says.
DIE WELT
- Liberal Free Democrats (FDP), junior coalition partners in governing coalition, launch fresh attacks on Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
- East German members of opposition Social Democrats (SPD) warn against alliance with former communist PDS.
- German industry hopes for revival in troubled peace process between Palestinians and Israel.
- Both sides in engineering industry gear up for strikes.
